title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

findings.explanation: The query parameter is used with Django ORM's icontains filter, which uses parameterized queries. No raw SQL is constructed.

The code calls get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() to filter mail_rules and mail_accounts. The test verifies this function correctly filters by owner (user1 sees own_account and unowned_account, but not other_account owned by user2). However, without seeing the implementation of get_objects_for_user_owner_aware(), we cannot confirm it properly enforces ownership checks in all cases. The test provides strong evidence the fix is working, but the implementation of the helper function is not visible in the diff.

evidence.content:
self.assertCountEqual(
            [account["id"] for account in response.data["mail_accounts"]],
            [own_account.id, unowned_account.id],
        )
        self.assertCountEqual(
            [rule["id"] for rule in response.data["mail_rules"]],
            [own_rule.id, unowned_rule.id],
        )

findings.suggested_fix: Verify that get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() correctly implements ownership filtering. The test shows expected behavior: user1 should see owned objects (own_account, own_rule) and unowned objects (unowned_account, unowned_rule), but not user2's objects (other_account, other_rule). Ensure the function checks both owner field (owner=user) and also handles unowned objects (owner=None) as accessible to all users with permission.
